answer.why_different: The generated document omits the entire `servers` declaration, causing a different address/structure: the official document declares a parameterized ProvMnS endpoint, while the generated document relies on OpenAPI's implicit default server URL `/`.
answer.spec_3gpp: The supplied 3GPP evidence describes the RESTful solution and operation mappings, but does not explicitly state the server declaration or its URL template.
answer.openapi: OpenAPI permits `servers` to be omitted, but omission changes the effective connectivity information: the default server has URL `/`. The official declaration provides the target URL and substitution variables for `MnSRoot`, `MnSVersion`, and `URI-LDN-first-part`.
answer.clearer_why: The official version clearly identifies the intended server endpoint and documents the variables needed to construct it. The generated version gives no equivalent endpoint information and instead leaves clients with the generic default `/`.

evidence.text: ### Specification Extensions While the OpenAPI Specification tries to accommodate most use cases, additional data can be added to extend the specification at certain points. The extensions properties are implemented as patterned fields that are always prefixed by `"x-"`. Field Pattern | Type | Description ---|:---:|--- ^x- | Any | Allows extensions to the OpenAPI Schema. The field name MUST begin with `x-`, for example, `x-internal-id`. The value can be `null`, a primitive, an array or an object. Can have any valid JSON format value. The extensions may or may not be supported by the available tooling, but those may be extended as well to add requested support (if tools are internal or open-sourced).
